title: The cone of an admissible monomorphism is homotopy equivalent to the quotient, and the triangle is isomorphic
author: The Stacks Project Authors

difficulty_reason: The counted unit is the author's own lemma lemma-cone-homotopy at source lines 4325-4379: in the standing situation, (1) an admissible short exact sequence x -> y -> z determines a homotopy equivalence e : C(alpha) -> z making the displayed diagram an isomorphism of triangles in the homotopy category, where x -> C(alpha) -> x[1] is the admissible sequence supplied by axiom (C); and (2) for an arbitrary morphism alpha : x -> y, using the factorisation of alpha through an admissible monomorphism given by the author's factorisation lemma, there is an isomorphism of triangles between the triangle of the factored sequence and the triangle of the cone of alpha. The proof at source lines 4381-4489 is a long explicit computation and is genuinely research-level in its bookkeeping. For part (1) it writes down a larger diagram without the sign change on the connecting map, defines the two maps e = beta p and f = b s - sigma delta explicitly, verifies by matrix computations that they are inverse up to homotopy (which consumes several identities among the structure maps, the differentials and the connecting morphisms), and then checks that the right square of the diagram commutes and that the resulting morphism of triangles is an isomorphism, referring to the earlier null-homotopy computation for the identity of a cone. Part (2) transfers the result across the factorisation. Every equality is a separate computation and the statement gives none of them. No cross-chapter result is invoked inside the retained span.
